Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Information Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Human Resources Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency across our 45 acute-care hospitals and 120 outpatient facilities in the Sunbelt and Midwest.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key aspects: initiatives to improve operating margin, operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, breakdown of revenue by service line, operating margin guidance for the next quarter and year, trends in staffing levels and contract labor usage, average reimbursement rates by payer category, revenue per admission trends and drivers, and percentage of revenue from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach to financial strength amid reimbursement pressures and labor challenges. Michael will provide much more detail on these shortly. Overall, we're positioning Horizon Health Partners at the upper quartile of our peers, driving sustainable growth and patient outcomes.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $2.59 billion, representing 90.8% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in labor productivity and supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.28 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year.

Let me dive deeper into those key aspects starting with our operating margin performance. For the quarter, we delivered a consolidated operating margin of 9.2%, marking a 140 basis point expansion year-over-year from 7.8%, and this represents our sixth straight quarter of sequential improvement, with a 70 basis point gain from Q2's 8.5%. This positions us at the upper quartile of public hospital peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare, who are around 8-10% amid labor and supply headwinds. Our trailing 12-month margin now stands at 8.7%.

The year-over-year dynamics reflect robust revenue growth of 8.2% to $2.85 billion, fueled by 5.7% higher patient days, 2.3% more admissions, and a 1.8% CMI rise to 1.92, especially in cardiology and orthopedics. Elective procedures rebounded to 105% of pre-pandemic levels, with outpatient surging 12%. Reimbursements benefited from a steady 2.4% Medicare IPPS update and commercial mix up to 42% from 39%, yielding 3.5% rate uplift from contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Anthem.

Expenses were controlled despite 5.2% wage inflation and 7% supply rises; labor cost per bed stabilized at $1,850 from $1,920 through 15% agency reductions via internal float pools. Supply savings hit $45 million via Vizient GPO on implants and contrast media, dropping non-labor to 28.4% of revenue with Epic EHR aiding RCM and AR days to 42. Southeast markets like Florida and Texas drove 14.2% margins from demographics and migration, while Midwest held at 9.8% despite uncompensated care.

Quarter-over-quarter, seasonal elective strength added CMI lift, with AI staffing from LeanTaaS hitting 92% OR utilization and supply controls shaving costs.

This margin expansion stems directly from our Margin Momentum 2025 initiative launched in Q4 2023, targeting 12% by year-end 2025. We've captured $285 million in annualized savings and uplift through nine months. Labor productivity, 45% of impact, used AI with Epic and ShiftMed to cut premium labor from 12% to 6% of payroll, saving $112 million YTD. RN productivity rose 15% to 5.2 patient-days per shift, localizing 85% travel nurses in Southeast amid 7% admission growth, and cross-training in Midwest boosted surgical techs 18%. Expect 200 bps more lift in 2025 from flu forecasting.

Supply chain, 25% of savings, aligned with HealthTrust for 12-15% discounts, consolidating SKUs to 28,000 with Omnicell RFID, saving $68 million including 9% surgical per-case cuts. Texas pharma rebates tied to outcomes, Midwest 340B expansions added 300 bps.

RCM and payer optimization, 20% uplift, cut denials to 7.2% with Cerner AI, AR to 42 days unlocking $45 million cash; commercial to 58%, CMI to 1.85 from ortho/cardio growth, Florida Optum contracts at 12.8% readmissions yielding $22 million savings.

Clinical efficiency, 10%, shortened ALOS to 4.3 days, OR to 78%, $50 million da Vinci investments cut complications 22%, outpatient to 42% mix with 18% ASC margins.

Synergies across pillars mitigate IPPS cuts and inflation; de novo Texas hospitals and $450 million CHS tuck-ins scale us up.

Now, on revenue breakdown by service line: Inpatient at $1.02 billion or 35.8%, up 4.5% but down 120 bps mix on outpatient shift; same-facility 3.2% from Southeast 6.2% growth, High-Acuity Hub for CMI lift. Outpatient $1.14 billion, 40%, up 14.7% with ASCs +18.2% post-$250 million acquisition, revenue per visit $1,450. ED/observation $430 million, 15.1%, +7.3% on 2.1 million visits; surgical standalone $180 million, 6.3%, +9.1% from transplants; behavioral/other $90 million, 3.2%, +28.4% on psych demand and home health JV.

Outpatient mix expansion accretes margins; de novo ASCs and VBC ahead.

Payer revenue percentage: Medicare 46.2% up from 44.8%, stable $14,200 per discharge despite MA denials via RCM; Medicaid 17.8% down from 19.2% on redeterminations, $8,450 per case; commercial 31.5% up slightly, $18,750 high margins from VBC; self-pay/other 4.5% compressed via charity.

Diversification with 78% Medicare/commercial supports resilience.

Average reimbursement rates: Overall ARPA $14,250, +3.1%; Medicare $11,800 +2.4% on IPPS, MA HCC 1.45; Medicaid $9,200 +4.1% SDPs; commercial $18,750 +2.8%, 132% Medicare; self-pay $15,400 flat, bad debt 2.1%. ASPD $2,450 +3.5%, AI appeals reverse 65% denials.

Revenue per admission $16,450 +5.2% YoY, CMI 1.92 +2.3% from TAVR/ortho, commercial 48%, Epic coding +$120, ancillaries +9%; Southeast $17,200, guide 5-5.5% FY24.

Staffing trends: 52,400 FTEs +3.2%, RNs 22,800 +4.1%, HPPD 8.4, turnover 18.4%; contract spend $285 million -38%, 11.2% labor vs 22%, bill rates $105/hr. Academy graduated 1,200, AI scheduling -22% OT; target sub-10% contract 2025.

Guidance: Q1 2025 7.2-7.8% from Q4 8.9%, labor/seasonal pressure offset by admissions +3-4%; FY25 8.0-8.5% + from 2024 via productivity, RCM $80 million, VBC 75 bps, ASCs. Full-year 2024 9.5-10.0%, Q4 10.5%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our bundled payment program has shown remarkable results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools that have improved early detection in cardiology by 20%.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-powered predictive scheduling and lean Six Sigma throughput processes, which have resulted in $50 million in cost savings, improved patient flow with ALOS down to 4.3 days, and enhanced staff productivity up 15% in high-volume units.

Next, Sarah Kline will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets like Texas and Florida with three de novo hospitals, enhance our service offerings through 15 new ASCs, and diversify our revenue streams via value-based contracts covering 25% of lives.

After that, Raj Patel will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures including AI threat detection and zero-trust architecture to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with HIPAA and HITECH, and mitigate the risk of data breaches following industry events like the Change Healthcare incident. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions with AWS and Azure to improve scalability and flexibility across our Epic ecosystem.

Following that, Karen Lopez will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Karen Lopez:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives including our Nursing Academy with 92% retention, merit pools at 5.5% tied to tenure bonuses averaging $128,000 RN comp, flexible scheduling pilots, and diversity programs that boosted underrepresented hires by 25%, fostering a culture of inclusion amid 18.4% turnover below peers.

Finally, David Ruiz will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

David Ruiz:
Thank you, Karen. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program including AI monitoring for fraud detection, regular HIPAA audits, and training reaching 100% of staff to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy under the No Surprises Act, and prevent fraud and abuse with denial rates managed proactively.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Karen Lopez:
Thanks, Jamie. Absolutely. Building on our progress, key initiatives include the HealthBridge Nursing Academy partnership with Chamberlain University, graduating 1,200 LPN-to-RN clinicians with 92% retention, saving $45 million in contract costs. We've enhanced total rewards with 5.5% merit increases, $10,000 sign-ons for critical roles, and flexible 36-hour scheduling to combat burnout. AI platforms like LeanTaaS have cut overtime 22%, improving work-life balance, while diversity training and engagement scores up 15% reflect our inclusive culture. These have driven turnover to 18.4%, with 85% nurse retention benchmarking above HCA's 82%. We're targeting further gains in 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

David Ruiz:
Great question, Lisa. Our comprehensive program includes AI-powered monitoring via Waystar and Optum for real-time fraud detection, quarterly HIPAA audits across all 45 hospitals, and 100% staff training on Stark Law and Anti-Kickback updates. Post-Change Healthcare, we've diversified RCM with Optum360 live in 70% of sites, stress-testing for breaches with zero incidents YTD. Collaborating with Raj's team on zero-trust and cloud encryption ensures HIPAA compliance, while advocacy on state levels addresses redetermination impacts. This mitigates risks like MA audits, keeping penalties at zero.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Reilly with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Mark Reilly:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, Mark. Our $450 million CHS tuck-in and $250 million ASC acquisitions add 18 facilities, immediately accretive at 18% EBITDA margins, mirroring Tenet's USP model. They boost Southeast density, driving 7% same-hospital growth from population inflows, and enable CMI lift via robotics in ortho/cardio. Pipeline includes $250 million more targeting Phoenix/Dallas ASCs, diversifying to 42% outpatient with VBC upside. Synergies with Margin Momentum yield 200 bps expansion, positioning for 15% EBITDA by 2027 amid MA growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Emily, thanks for the question. Our AI-powered diagnostic tools, integrated with Epic and Cerner RevCycle, enhance accuracy in cardiology and oncology by analyzing imaging for TAVR candidates, achieving 22% complication reductions akin to da Vinci outcomes. Predictive analytics forecast acuity for staffing, while telehealth triage cuts ED boarding 30%. In neuro, Nuance Dragon boosts CC/MCC capture, supporting CMI 1.92. Early results show 20% faster detections, aligning with CMS quality metrics for VBC shared savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you expand on Q4 margin guidance risks and opportunities?

Michael Chen:
Sure, David. Q4 at 10.5% assumes 2% volume upside from electives, but risks include 2.8% IPPS cuts and 4-5% wage inflation. Opportunities from RCM AI preventing 10% denials, supply GPO savings, and ASC shift add 100 bps. If flu moderates, we exceed high end; stable acuity supports FY24 9.5-10.0%.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
